records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this plant. In case PU-24-342 at the North Dakota Public Service Commission, Northern States Power, doing business as Xcel Energy, must build a gas plant of at least 200 MW in eastern North Dakota. Its supplemental filing of August 5, 2025 says it bid 447 MW of firm dispatchable capacity directly adjacent to the Xcel Energy Bison Substation in Harmony Township, Cass County, about 10 miles west of Fargo. The project chart in that filing shows service in the third quarter of 2032. Xcel says it has already spent about 1.6 million dollars on site design, surveys, land options and MISO study payments. The timeline in the filing has the revised plant proposed in 2027, an interconnection agreement and a certificate filing in 2029, construction in 2030 and service late in 2032. The commission order of October 23, 2025 moved the deadline to December 31, 2032. MISO queue entry J3163 is the same project: Northern States Power, Cass County, 481 MW simple cycle combustion turbine, connecting at Bison. The filing gives 447 MW, so that is the capacity used. The status is announced because no certificate application or interconnection agreement exists yet. The point is the Bison Substation, so the location is approximate. The name is chosen to keep it apart from Basin Electric's Bison Generation Station in Williams County. GEM's Xcel Fargo power plant record is a cancelled 400 MW project from an earlier plan. A separate question card covers it.

records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list a gas plant at Coal Creek. Rainbow Energy Center owns the Coal Creek coal plant near Underwood in McLean County. Its presentation to a North Dakota legislative committee on September 10, 2025 lists 2+ GW of new natural gas generation at Coal Creek as a growth plan. The same slide set says Rainbow is in exclusive talks with a data center developer on a 2.1 GW power purchase agreement and has 800 acres zoned. A Minot Daily News story of April 15, 2026 says Rainbow is looking to add gas generation and expects 2.1 gigawatts to be available, fed by a new 136 mile, 36 inch pipeline due in 2029. A POWER magazine article from July 2025 says the same plan is under consideration. No buyer has signed, no air permit or commission case was found, and no turbine, unit count or start year is given. The capacity is the 2,000 MW floor the company states. The point is the Coal Creek plant, so the location is approximate. The status is announced on the company's own planning document.
